messages:
anya: Quick sync — ran a short experiment combining a lazy rolling-window KV-cache + a reroll sampling strategy on llama3-12b (q4_0). Sharing raw numbers and a proposed ablation plan, would love quick takes.

ciara: Nice, can you paste the perf delta? latency and tokens/s? :eyes:

anya: Baseline (no lazy, greedy):
- throughput: 42 tok/s
- p95 latency: 210ms

Lazy-window only (window_size=32, stride=8):
- throughput: 62 tok/s (+48%)
- p95: 240ms

Lazy + reroll (top_k->reroll top-2, n_samples=3):
- throughput: 58 tok/s
- p95: 260ms

So overall token throughput improved vs baseline; p95 regressed a bit vs baseline but still within our soft SLO for these setups.

rahul: What about quality? which eval set?

anya: Ran on our in-house 1k eval (mix: summarization 40%, instruction-follow 40%, code completion 20%). Quick metrics: exact_match (code) dropped 0.7 points, instr-follow helpfulness score down ~1.5 points, rouge-L on summarization ~0.4 down. Safety/hallucination probes didn't spike.

ciara: hmm small regressions but throughput win is decent. Did you keep prefix caching enabled?

anya: Yes prefix_cache: true. Also used the continuous-batcher with batch_size cap 64. Command used: \n```
run-bench --model=llama3-12b --quant=q4_0 --workers=16 --config=experiments/lazy_reroll.yaml
```
And the bench output tail: \n```
[bench] started workers=16
[bench] steady-state tok/s=58
[bench] p95=260ms
```

ciara: Can you paste the config snippet?

anya: Sure:
```
lazy_window:
  enabled: true
  window_size: 32
  stride: 8
  max_cached_tokens: 1024
reroll_sampling:
  enabled: true
  top_k_reroll: 2
  n_samples: 3
  temperature: 0.8
  reroll_on_confidence_below: 0.25
decode:
  max_new_tokens: 256
  early_stop: false
quant: q4_0
```

eva: Quick thought: rerolling on every token will blow up compute; looks like you used a threshold — good. Did you reroll across all tokens or only at sentence boundaries / low-prob tokens?

anya: Implemented reroll_on_confidence_below=0.25 so only triggers on low-prob tokens. In practice ~12% of tokens triggered reroll, with n_samples=3, which explains the slight p95 hit.

rahul: For quality regressions we should check: 1) whether reroll reduces mode-seeking helpfulness (e.g., leverages more diverse outputs but less targeted), 2) whether quantization interacts badly with sampling. Did you run fp16 baseline?

anya: fp16 baseline (no quant) with lazy-window gave throughput ~85 tok/s and similar small quality drop vs our origin. We focused on q4_0 because it's our realistic serving target; quant seems to amplify small sampling instability.

ciara: Suggest running ablation matrix: top_k_reroll {1,2,4}, n_samples {1,3,5}, reroll_on_confidence {0.1,0.25,0.4}, and an arm that only rerolls at whitespace boundaries vs any low-prob token. Keep lazy_window fixed.

anya: Agreed. Proposed quick plan:
- Phase A (smoke, 100 prompts): run all combos but n_samples max 3 to keep cost low.
- Phase B (1000 prompts): run promising combos (top_k=1 or 2, n_samples 3/5) and full eval suite.
- Phase C: safety/hallucination stress with targeted prompts.

eva: Also add a run with reroll disabled but with higher temp (0.9) and top_k adjusted to compare diversity-vs-reroll tradeoffs.

rahul: One more: try conditional reroll only for tokens where the top-1 prob < X AND next_token_entropy > Y — could reduce unnecessary rerolls.

anya: Good call. I'll add an extra metric to log per-token top1_prob and entropy when reroll triggers. Quick log example: \n```
[token] idx=14 top1=0.18 entropy=3.8 reroll_triggered=true
[token] idx=15 top1=0.72 entropy=1.1 reroll_triggered=false
```

ciara: Sounds solid. If Phase A looks promising, we should farm out runs on dedicated-reserved infra (lower noise) for Phase B.

deploy-bot: deployment reminder: dedicated cluster rr-run-3 has free slots 03:00-08:00 UTC, ask SRE for reservation.

anya: Will schedule Phase A tonight, tag results here. Thanks for the feedback. :rocket: 

eva: Nice — please include per-case p95 and the instr-follow nudge tests. Also add a small human eval for the top 50 instr-follow outputs (blind).

rahul: If we see consistent quality drop with q4_0 + reroll, next step is to try q5_1 (mixed-precision) or restrict reroll to sampled beam candidates instead of n_samples from the model.

ciara: One-liner: promising perf wins, small quality regressions; we can likely recover via smarter trigger heuristics. :thumbsup:

anya: Agreed. I'll post Phase A results tomorrow morning with the ablation table and raw logs attached.
